title: Normalized ringed-site duality model and coefficient unit
statement: Let $C$ be a category with object universe $c$ and morphism universe $v$, let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on $C$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings in universe $\max(c,v,r)$. Use the sheaf-of-modules category of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheafification and local-bijection identification for additive sheaves in that universe, and a derived category in universe $w$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A normalized ringed-site duality model is the following data, with no existence assertion: a closed tensor-Hom structure and its K-flat pure-tensor representative normalization [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], a symmetric structure on that same tensor, and an isomorphism from its tensor unit to $R[0]$. Here $R[0]$ is the derived image of the coefficient module concentrated in cochain degree zero. The model includes K-flatness of this coefficient complex [def-pc-kflat-complex]. It requires that the symmetry on K-flat representatives descend the signed interchange $x_p\otimes y_q\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y_q\otimes x_p$, that the right unitor descend scalar multiplication $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, and that the associator descend $(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$, using the representative isomorphisms of the same tensor-Hom model. All cochain degrees are integers. The definition assumes neither perfectness nor invertibility of bidual or evaluation maps.
